evidence.excerpt: This paper presents a quantitative framework for evaluating boundary-scan controllability and observability on mixed-signal printed circuit board assemblies where analogue subcircuits interrupt digital scan chains. The method assigns a weighted coverage score to each net segment based on the ratio of scan-accessible driver–receiver pairs to the total number of electrical nodes. Experiments were conducted on three reference boards populated with 128, 256, and 512 component pins respectively, using a commercial JTAG controller operating at 10 MHz TCK. Coverage scores were compared against hand-calculated fault-injection results for twelve common defect classes including opens, shorts, and stuck-at faults. The framework identified a 14–22 % gap between nominal boundary-scan coverage estimates and empirically verified detection rates on nets that cross analogue power domains. A correction factor derived from net impedance profiles is proposed and validated on an automotive-grade sensor interface board. The approach requires no modifications to existing IEEE 1149.1 infrastructure.
